item.title: Trade grades for Jaguars-Falcons deal for Jessie Bates
item.description: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is just over 24 hours away. And Monday morning delivered the latest big deal as teams try and improve ahead of the push for the playoffs. The Jacksonville Jaguars made a move to shore up the back of the secondary, pulling off a trade for safety Jessie Bates III of the Atlanta Falcons. Here are the full terms of the deal: Jaguars receive: Jessie Bates III Falcons receive: 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick Let’s hand out some grades. Jaguars grade for Jessie Bates trade The Jaguars look like one of the NFL’s elite teams. Heading into Week 10, Jacksonville sits at 6-2, three games ahead of the Houston Texans in the AFC South. The Jaguars are a likely playoff team, and have some metrics to back up their elite status. Jacksonville is tops in the NFL with a point differential of +108, and when you look at “Team Tiers,” which examines both offenses and defenses through the lens of Expected Points Added, the Jaguars are on par with the San Francisco 49ers at the head of the pack : So it is probably no surprise that general manager James Gladstone is going to be aggressive ahead of the NFL trade deadline. With the Jaguars in a clear window to contend, making a move like this makes a good deal of sense. And word out of Jacksonville in recent days held that the Jaguars were looking for “defensive playmakers,” and Bates certainly fits that description. And with Atlanta paying most of the contract , that helps put this deal in a more favorable light for Jacksonville. What brings the grade down a bit is the contract situation. Bates is in the final year of his contract, and is set to be an unrestricted free agent in 2027. This could mean he is a one-year rental for the Jaguars, which has to factor into the equation. Now, if Jacksonville were to sign him to a new deal, that would certainly bump the grade up a bit, but the contact has to play a role in the equation here. Jaguars grade: B (which can improve with some extra credit, i.e., signing Bates to an extension). Falcons grade for Jessie Bates trade On the one hand, it is something of a head-scratcher to see Atlanta trade away a key defensive player, given the fact that the Falcons are still in the thick of things in the NFC South playoff race. If the NFC South playoff race could be described as such. Atlanta sits at 3-6, at the bottom of the division. But they are not far behind the first-place Carolina Panthers (who clock in at 3-5) and with a win over the Panthers already this season, there is a case that Atlanta should be buying rather than selling. But with Bates set to hit free agency, this might be the best opportunity to get something for him beyond a compensatory selection, and a second-round pick in 2027 and a fifth-round pick in 2028 is a nice little return. item.title: Falcons trade Jessie Bates to Jaguars
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 25: Jessie Bates III #3 of the Atlanta Falcons reacts after an interception during the third quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off their fourth loss in five games, the Atlanta Falcons will be a seller at the trade deadline, moving safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second round pick and 2028 fifth round pick. The team’s huge free agency splash in 2023 is gone after a fantastic run in Atlanta that spanned about three-and-a-half seasons, and the Falcons are loading up to try and remake their roster in 2027. The Jacksonville Jaguars are trading for Falcons S Jessie Bates III, sources tell @TheAthletic . The Jags are sending a 2027 2nd round pick and 2028 5th to Atlanta acquire Bates. A big move by one of the NFL’s top teams ahead of the deadline. — Jonathan Jones (@jjones9) November 9, 2026 Per Jonathan Jones, who I cited above, the Falcons will eat some of the contract to facilitate a move. That’s not surprising given that they’re going to be sitting on plenty of cap space next year and clearly want more early draft selections for next year and beyond. With Bates moving to Jacksonville, I’d have to expect that DeMarcco Hellams, Sydney Brown, or both will be taking on his snaps next to Xavier Watts, but we’ll get more clarity on that in the week ahead. For the moment, let’s appreciate what Bates gave the Falcons while he was here. Few safeties in franchise history were more impactful than Bates, who had 14 interceptions, three interceptions returned for touchdowns, 11 forced fumbles, and a fumble returned for a touchdown in his time in Atlanta. While he was typically solid-to-excellent in coverage and provided sure tackling throughout his tenure, the big plays were why the Falcons signed him and the big plays were worth every penny. He was a game changing player who lifted lousy defenses and headline great ones, and it goes without saying that this will be a greatly diminished Falcons defense in 2026 without him. I’ll miss watching him play for my favorite team, and I’m grateful we got to do so for the past four years. The Falcons looked at the writing on the wall for their 2026 and clearly felt their chances of making a real run were not worth as much as the long-term lift they could get from another second round pick next year; time will tell as always whether that calculus was the right one. It will be incumbent on a front office that has had some promising signings and trades to make sure that trading away a safety as good as Bates doesn’t come back to haunt them. In the short term, as I said above, I’d expect run for Hellams and Brown. item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Tim Parker played his last professional game on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The 33-year-old defender stepped onto the field at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, New Jersey, for one final match. He came on in the 90th minute to replace Sekou Kone during a 3-0 victory over Atlanta United. The crowd watched a local boy finish his career with a win, playing into the third minute of stoppage time before the final whistle blew. This was not just a game; it was the end of a 12-year journey through Major League Soccer. Parker, a native of Hicksville, New York, played 304 league matches in total. He chose to leave the sport on his own terms after a decade of hard work. The Red Bull New York team honored him by handing him the captain’s armband for this farewell performance. A Career Built on Hard Work Parker’s path to the top was not easy. He spent five years with Vancouver, making 100 appearances and scoring four goals. In 2015, he helped his team win the Canadian Championship. His time in Houston came next, where he played for two seasons and served as co-captain for both 2021 and 2022. He also spent two seasons with St. Louis CITY SC, scoring six goals there, including the very first goal in the club’s history. His most successful stretch came with the Red Bulls, where he played five seasons and made 128 appearances across all competitions. This number is higher than his time with any other club. In his first year with New York in 2018, he helped the team win the Supporters Shield. That same year, the club set a record for the most points in a single MLS season. The defense Parker anchored allowed only 33 goals, which was the fewest in the league. They also kept 15 clean sheets, the highest total in the league that year. Bradley explained that the way Parker treated his teammates made him a proud figure in the dressing room. The official statement from the club confirmed that Parker’s impact extends well beyond what he accomplished on the field. item.title: Grades: Lions’ defensive dominance overshadows OL struggles
item.description: In the standings, style points do not count. The Detroit Lions’ 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins counts the same as if the Lions had blown the Dolphins out 38-3. But in our weekly report cards, we only talk style points. We examine the good and the bad, because life isn’t really just a binary of wins and losses. So let’s hand out some mediocre grades in the Lions’ Week 9 victory. Quarterback: D+ Jared Goff wasn’t exceptionally bad in this game, but there was probably more bad than good. He was put into some tough positions early with pressure coming from seemingly every angle. It’s hard to fault him for the interception when his arm was hit while throwing, but Goff also didn’t handle the pressure particularly well in this game. There are two plays in which I think illustrate Goff’s self-made struggles in this game. The first was Detroit’s run-back of the CFL-like play with Amon-Ra St. Brown 15 yards behind the line of scrimmage. The play successfully distracted the Dolphins defense from aptly covering Jahmyr Gibbs’ wheel route of the backfield, but Goff, under mild pressure, didn’t make that throw and checked it down instead. Then, late in the game, the Lions faced a third-and-7 from the Dolphins 25-yard line. With a defender in his face, Goff tried to hit St. Brown on an out route. When at his best, Goff steps into that throw knowing he’s going to get hit and delivers a perfect ball. On Sunday, feeling the effects of the pressure, Goff faded away and delivered a ball several feet beyond St. Brown’s reach. Again, not a horrible day from Goff, but below average certainly. Running backs: C- I thought the running backs did a decent job in pass protection, but there weren’t any standout plays in which it felt like they created any yardage on their own. The Lions managed just 1.55 yards after contract on Sunday, the second-lowest mark of any team in Week 9. This unit certainly wasn’t helped by the offensive line for much of this game, but I still left the game wanting more from Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki. Tight ends: C- Last week’s “sidecar” formation—with two tight ends in the backfield—was so successful vs. the Vikings. On Sunday, it didn’t seem to have the same effectiveness. There were several times it felt like the tight ends weren’t getting the push they got last week, and I think that impacted both the run and pass game. That said, Sam LaPorta was an effective receiver that I wish Detroit had targeted more. He caught four of his five targets for 32 yards—though he also had a false start penalty. But it was really Amon-Ra St. Brown’s afternoon. He was the team’s best offensive player on Sunday, constantly finding room in the Dolphins’ zone coverage. item.title: WWE Superstars managed to leave Saudi Arabia before latest attack in Riyadh
item.description: Photo by Andrew Timms/WWE via Getty Images After immense security concerns regarding their Crown Jewel PLE in Saudi Arabia, the WWE ensured their talent was escorted out of the country safely. Given the tense geopolitical situation in the Middle East, many organisations, including the U.S. Department of State, cautioned WWE from holding their Crown Jewel show in Saudi Arabia. However, TKO officials trudged along with their plans to host the show, albeit changing plans to use a venue with a smaller capacity to ensure safety, and airing it with a 15-minute delay. WWE managed to get Superstars out of Saudi Arabia before Sunday attack in Riyadh According to Mike Johnson of PWInsider , all WWE Superstars had been ‘long gone’ before the latest attack in Riyadh on Sunday. However, he did add that there were likely some production staff members in the country to help take down the set of the PLE. “For those who have asked about the news… the WWE roster was long gone before the attack happened. There would still be some WWE staff in the city, likely those helping to break down the arena and production, but we have not heard of anyone associated to the company being affected.” To avoid any issues for their superstars, WWE coordinated travel to Saudi Arabia via road from Bahrain, as the Riyadh airport had been targeted in previous attacks. The show itself went off relatively smoothly, with no security issues. However, WWE took precautions, limiting the number of stars they brought to the show and limiting the matches and overall runtime of the show to help get everyone out of the country as soon as possible. Even though there were no issues from a security standpoint, WWE find themselves receiving more backlash for even hosting the event there in the first place. For many fans, the sentiment is that the WWE (and TKO as a whole) prioritised their profits over the safety of their Superstars. And on top of that, albeit not as much of a concern, the quality of the show was also incredibly poor, with results, performances, and stars receiving negative reception from the fans in attendance and online. item.description: Sunday’s FA Cup first-round action delivered major upsets as Oldham Athletic dumped Sheffield Wednesday out with a dramatic extra-time winner in Dave Challinor’s first game in charge of the Owls. There was further misery for Crawley Town, who suffered a shock defeat against seventh-tier Wimborne Town to exit the competition at the first-round stage for the second successive season. Stockport County produced a remarkable comeback to avoid an upset against Cray Wanderers, recovering from two goals down and a red card to win 3-2 after extra time. Finally, Grimsby Town survived a major scare against eighth-tier Stafford Rangers, coming from two goals down to draw 3-3 after extra time before eventually booking their place in the second round with a penalty shootout victory. Here’s how the EFL sides fared in Sunday’s first-round ties. The homegrown central defender was up for a free-kick which the Owls failed to clear, with Sutton left completely free to nod home from six yards and secure a 2-1 win. After an uneventful first three quarters of the match, it suddenly exploded into life. Calum Kavanagh put Oldham ahead in the 66th minute with a fierce drive after Mike Fondop headed on Noah Chilvers’ right-wing cross – his sixth goal of the season. Wednesday equalised 10 minutes later through former Oldham forward Davis Keillor-Dunn. The Wrexham loanee found the bottom corner with a shot from a cross by substitute Sean Fusire, his fifth of the campaign for the League One side. Oldham manager Micky Mellon was sent off and Sheffield Wednesday player Callum Slattery booked. After Sutton’s winning goal, Oldham defended resolutely to close out the game. item.description: Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Baltimore Ravens in Week 9 and were clear buyers for the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Sitting comfortably atop the AFC South, the Jaguars needed some help. Looking at this roster, two main needs came into focus: defensive tackle and safety. While they've yet to make a move in the DT market, the Jaguars have reportedly made their safety move, and it's a massive one. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Jaguars are sending the Atlanta Falcons two draft picks to acquire Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates, one of the best safeties in the NFL, to get a major upgrade on the defensive side of the ball. Jaguars to acquire Jessie Bates from Falcons for two picks "Trade: Falcons are sending former Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick, sources tell ESPN," Schefter reports. This is a massive move for the Jaguars prior to the Tuesday trade deadline, as Bates is one of the best defensive backs in the NFL and was one of the more intriguing trade candidates seemingly available this season. He's a 29-year-old safety who was a Pro Bowler one time back in 2023. While he might not have a lot of accolades, Bates is an incredible DB who will be a major upgrade in Jacksonville. This season for the Falcons, Bates has 60 total tackles with one fumble returned for a touchdown, three forced fumbles, one interception, and three passes defended. There might not have been a better safety on the trade block this season than Bates, and James Gladstone is swinging big with this major acquisition. It's a big trade, as the Jaguars giving up a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick isn't a cheap package to give up for a rental DB. But with a real chance of winning the Super Bowl, the Jaguars are going all in. item.title: Friedel group completes Shrewsbury Town takeover
item.description: Roland Wycherley has been Shrewsbury Town owner and chairman since 1996 [Shrewsbury Town FC] Shrewsbury Town's long-drawn-out takeover deal has been completed, allowing former USA international goalkeeper Brad Friedel to come in as the Shropshire outfit's new sporting director. The paperwork on the share purchase agreement with Scott Davidson's American-based consortium Biscayne ST LLC - which includes Friedel - has been finalised, taking up 87.4 per cent of the League Two club's shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to finally let go. Miami-based businessman Davidson is joined on the new Town board by New York financier Will Dotson and Craig Graham, chairman of Spartans, the Edinburgh-based Scottish League Two club, while former Liverpool, Blackburn Rovers, Aston Villa and Tottenham Hotspur keeper Friedel will come in to take a hands-on role, working with manager Gavin Cowan. Davidson becomes chairman of the board, which still includes existing members Liam Dooley, the club's chief executive, and Duncan Montgomery, while another ex-goalkeeper, Bryan Finnerty, is to join the group, pending the EFL's owners and directors' tests. After 30 years of leading the Shropshire club, since succeeding Ray Bailey as chairman in the summer of 1996, Wycherley can now retire at the age of 85. The Shrewsbury-born lifelong fan first made his intention clear to sell more than five years ago when the Town were still a League One club. But his dogged determination to do a deal he had to be convinced was right for the club's long-term future before he handed over the reins has made the Shropshire businessman a tough adversary - and lengthened the process, to the frustration of Town fans. In a club statement, Wycherley said his ownership tenure had been "an honour and a privilege" but admitted the club "needed new investment". Shrewsbury take step closer to takeover deal Shrewsbury chairman's succession plan We took our time, says Shrewsbury Town owner Wycherley After suffering relegation in his first season, Shrewsbury have since been relegated three more times - and promoted three times - in Wycherley's period as owner. But the biggest legacy of his three decades at the helm was the Town's move in 2007 from their old Gay Meadow home to a new 10,000 all-seater stadium. The first of those three promotions was under Graham Turner, who returned to the club to recreate the success they had in the late 1970s and early 1980s, taking them up in 2012. "Roland has put an awful lot into the football club," Turner told BBC Radio Shropshire. "He's kept it going, when at times it's been hard. "I've nothing but admiration for him. Over the years he's done a very good job." Wycherley's last game watching the club while at the helm was Saturday's 2-1 FA Cup first-round win at non-league Eastleigh. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Andre Drummond did not score against Cleveland, and the Knicks still got valuable minutes from their backup center. That matters for a team trying to keep its starters effective across a long season. In 14 minutes of Saturday’s 109-97 win, Drummond collected eight rebounds, including two offensive boards, with two steals and a block. New York outscored Cleveland by 10 while he was on the floor, according to the NBA box score . Nov 4, 2026; New York, New York, USA; New York Knicks center Andre Drummond (0) controls the ball against Chicago Bulls forward Leonard Miller (11) and guard Tre Jones (30) during the third quarter at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Knicks can win minutes without extra scoring Drummond took only one shot. The value came from ending possessions, giving New York another chance on the glass and covering a stretch without asking Karl-Anthony Towns to play the entire game. I would keep a defined rebounding role for Drummond against bigger second units, especially on nights when Towns needs a breather. Extra possessions are useful, and a reserve center does not need a high usage rate to justify his minutes. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. The tradeoff is spacing. A Towns-led lineup can pull a center away from the basket in a way a traditional reserve lineup may not. Coaches can also use smaller groups against opponents who spread the floor and force repeated defensive rotations. Single-game plus-minus is noisy and does not prove Drummond alone caused the margin. The eight rebounds and the team’s ability to survive those minutes are a more useful starting point for deciding where his role fits. item.title: Yankees face a closer choice with a $23 million deadline
item.description: Oct 7, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees pitcher David Bednar (53) throws during the ninth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game three of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Yankees should not assume David Bednar’s future will take care of itself while other closers come off the board. His decision on a $23.15 million qualifying offer is approaching, and the alternative could cost New York something entirely different: young talent. Milwaukee closer Trevor Megill has entered the trade discussion. Pinstripes Nation’s Sara Molnick relayed Joel Sherman’s assessment that the Brewers could explore his market. The assessment does not report that New York is currently negotiating a deal. Oct 5, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; New York Yankees pitcher David Bednar (53) delivers a pitch during the eighth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game two of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Yankees need more than one bullpen plan Bednar converted 35 saves with a 2.47 ERA over 69 1/3 innings in 2026. New York extended the qualifying offer, which he must accept or reject by November 17; a rejection would not prevent the sides from negotiating a longer deal. Megill saved 30 games for Milwaukee and recorded the final six outs of its championship-clinching World Series win. A trade could provide late-inning experience, but any prospect cost would come on top of his salary and the risk attached to acquiring a reliever. I would keep talking to Bednar and ask Milwaukee about Megill’s price without treating either pitcher as a guaranteed solution. Re-signing Bednar preserves prospects; acquiring Megill could leave more flexibility on the contract side, depending on the actual terms. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. Neither choice fills every opening. Paul Blackburn and several other Yankees relievers also reached free agency, so paying for a closer cannot be the entire winter plan. No public asking price or current Yankees offer is established, and Bednar may accept the one-year deal before a trade becomes necessary. item.description: จัดอันดับ 10 เว็บไซต์ แทงบอลสเต็ป น่าเล่น ไม่มีลิมิต จ่ายเต็มทุกคู่ สมัครสมาชิก กดที่นี่ มองหา เว็บแทงบอลสเต็ป ที่จ่ายหนัก จ่ายจริง ไม่มีลิมิต จ่ายเต็มทุกคู่ อยู่ใช่ไหม? ปี 2026 นี้เราได้มัดรวม 10 อันดับ เว็บแทงบอลสเต็ป ที่ดีที่สุดมาให้คุณแบบเน้นๆ การันตีความปลอดภัยด้วยระบบเว็บตรง ไม่ผ่านเอเย่นต์ มั่นใจได้กับอัตราต่อรองที่ดีที่สุดและยอดจ่ายเต็มจำนวนทุกบิล ไม่ว่าคุณจะเป็นเซียนบอลชุดหรือมือใหม่ ก็สามารถเริ่มต้นทำกำไรได้อย่างไร้ขีดจำกัดพร้อมบริการฝากถอนวอเลทและธนาคารชั้นนำด้วยระบบออโต้ตลอด 24 ชั่วโมง รีวิว 10 เว็บแทงบอลสเต็ป น่าเล่นที่สุดในไทย ค่าน้ำดี ไม่มีลิมิต จ่ายเต็มทุกคู่ คัดเน้นๆ 10 เว็บแทงบอลสเต็ป เว็บตรงแท้ ยอดนิยมในปี 2026 ที่เหล่านักเดิมพันให้การยอมรับว่าเป็น เว็บตรงลิขสิทธิ์แท้ จากต่างประเทศ ไม่ผ่านเอเย่นต์ มอบค่าน้ำดีที่สุด ไม่มีลิมิตในการแทงบอลออนไลน์ และการันตีระบบการเงินมั่นคงจ่ายเต็มทุกยอดบิล พร้อมรวบรวมข้อมูลสำคัญ รีวิวเจาะลึก และแนวทางการเล่นที่ปลอดภัย เพื่อให้คุณเริ่มต้นทำกำไรจากบอลชุดได้อย่างมั่นใจและไร้ความกังวลตลอด 24 ชั่วโมง 1. UFA246 UFA246 เหมาะกับผู้ที่ต้องการเปรียบเทียบตลาดฟุตบอลและจัดบิล แทงบอลสเต็ป ผ่านระบบออนไลน์ หน้าเดิมพันของ เว็บแทงบอลไม่มีขั้นต่ํา ช่วยให้ตรวจสอบคู่แข่งขัน ราคา และประเภทการเดิมพันก่อนจัดบิลได้สะดวก สำหรับคนที่สงสัยว่า แทงบอลสเต็ป คิดเงินยังไง ควรดูอัตราต่อรองของแต่ละคู่และผลการแข่งขันที่เข้าเงื่อนไขครบทุกคู่ ควรอ่านรายละเอียดการเดิมพันและเงื่อนไขการรับเดิมพันก่อนยืนยันทุกครั้ง เพื่อให้เข้าใจยอดรับตามระบบอย่างชัดเจน ขั้นตอนการสมัคร เข้าสู่เมนู “ลงทะเบียน” หน้าเว็บหลัก UFA246 ใส่หมายเลขโทรศัพท์ 10 หลักเพื่อยืนยันตัวตน กรอกข้อมูลส่วนตัวและเลขที่บัญชีสำหรับการฝาก-ถอน กำหนดรหัสผ่านสำหรับการเข้าใช้งานระบบ กดยืนยันข้อมูลเพื่อรับยูสเซอร์และเริ่มแทงบอล สเต็ปได้เลย 3. UFAPLUS UFAPLUS เป็นอีกตัวเลือกสำหรับผู้ที่สนใจ แทงบอลสเต็ป และต้องการระบบที่รองรับการจัดหลายคู่ไว้ในโพยเดียว จุดที่น่าสนใจของ เว็บ แทงบอลสเต็ป ออนไลน์ คือ ในเครือข่ายเดียวกับ เว็บแทงบอลยูฟ่าเบท มีตลาดฟุตบอลหลายรูปแบบให้เลือกตามการแข่งขันที่เปิดรับเดิมพัน สำหรับ สอนแทงบอลสเต็ป มือใหม่ ควรเริ่มจากการทำความเข้าใจประเภทเดิมพัน อัตราต่อรอง และวิธีตรวจสอบบิลก่อนเล่นจริง นอกจากนี้ควรเปรียบเทียบราคาและเงื่อนไขของแต่ละคู่ เพื่อเลือกตลาดที่ตรงกับความเข้าใจของตัวเองมากที่สุด ขั้นตอนการสมัคร คลิกปุ่ม “สมัครเว็บแทงบอล” บนหน้าเว็บไซต์ UFAPLUS กรอกเบอร์มือถือของคุณเพื่อทำรายการ ระบุชื่อ-นามสกุล และเลือกธนาคารที่ต้องการผูกบัญชี ตั้งค่ารหัสผ่านส่วนตัวสำหรับเข้าสู่ระบบเดิมพัน ตรวจสอบคว

item.description: TAIPEI, TAIWAN - SEPTEMBER 12: Shoki Oda #11 of Team Japan interacts with Ritora Yamada #2 of Team Japan in the first inning during the BFA U18 Asian Baseball Championship Super Round game between Chinese Taipei and Japan at Taipei Dome on September 12, 2026 in Taipei, Taiwan. (Photo by Gene Wang - Capture At Media/Getty Images) | Getty Images Japanese right-hander Shoki Oda is one of the most interesting names of the offseason, as the 18-year-old right-hander is meeting with MLB teams, including the Dodgers . The lure of a larger bonus in the U.S. than what they might get in the NPB draft has led to some Japanese teenagers to jump stateside. Yuri Karasawa talked about this trend as well as Oda as a guest of Ben Lindbergh on an episode of the Effectively Wild Podcast last week . Karasawa went deeper into Oda with Jordan Shusterman and Jake Mintz on the Baseball Bar-B-Cast podcast . Eric Longenhagen at FanGraphs scouted several Japanese players available this winter , and wrote, “My sources tell me Oda is more likely to sign after the new international signing period begins in 2027 rather than try to sneak in before the end of 2026.” Aaron Bates and the Dodgers couldn’t come to an agreement on a contract extension which led to the hitting coach and the team parting ways last week after a dozen years coaching in the organization. Bates told Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times he was initially surprised by the split , but otherwise took the high road: “Processing it, I think that there’s always a time and a place, and I think that things run their course,” Bates said. “But I have nothing but amazing things to say about the Dodgers organization and people.” Ken Rosenthal and Evan Drellich at The Athletic spoke to several baseball agents , who are aligned with one another on at least one thing — MLB should not have a salary cap. This quote is from Rafa Nieves, agent of Teoscar Hernández and others: “The league proposals, and the way they are trying to bully the players, have united them,” Nieves said. “A year or two ago, I would have maybe answered differently. … But when you come up with these proposals, just insulting them, it is going to wrangle them together. Which is what I have noticed: They’re more united, they’re more together, they’re getting more informed.”

item.title: Blackburn Rovers 2-1 West Ham - the fans' verdict
item.description: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Blackburn Rovers beat West Ham 2-1 at Ewood Park in the Championship on Saturday. Here are some of your comments: Blackburn fans Keith: Typical Rovers, always play better against fancied teams but a good rehearsal for our next match against somebody else in claret and blue. One new manager bounce overcome. Let's hope for another next time out. Ronnie: West Ham thought they just had to turn up and Blackburn would roll over. Well that went well for them. Rob: A team that has more chance of going up than West Ham. They certainly had West Ham's mark. Vicky: Perfect day - Rovers win and Burnley lose from 4-1 up. Jeff: Actually inspiring from Rovers for once. Tony has done a great job so far, and a great atmosphere at the end. We turned the pressure on us in the first half to a win- so well done lads. John: I can honestly say it's the best Rovers game I've seen for a long time, they played their hearts out. As Rovers fan I couldn't be more chuffed for the way they stuck together, and showed such grit and determination. And it paid off. West Ham fans Clive: A new manager can't improve players that are not good enough to put a West Ham shirt on their backs. At least six players are not good enough to play in the Championship. West Ham will not get promotion until you change the core squad. One chance - January transfer window. Paul: Not good enough. I remember last time we went down we just managed to win promotion through the play-offs. Same thing this time, I fear. Sue: Played better but still don't take their chances. We could have won easily if they had taken their chances when they were in the box. Definitely need a centre forward. Got to keep confident and give Scott Parker a chance. He's only had four days. Ewan: West Ham were clearly not clinical in the final third, Blackburn defended brilliantly and West Ham's wingers could not get past Blackburn's full-backs. Simply not good enough from a West Ham perspective. Nigel: Hopefully reality is dawning on a squad full of ego and delusions of grandeur. They need to go back to basics, many weren't good enough for the Premier League and are now being found out in the Championship. A root and branch update is needed and Scotty should take the opportunity to ring serious changes during this international break. If we do not go up at the first time of asking I fear our stay in this division will be a prolonged one. Sofian: It was actually a decent performance compared to recent weeks. We pressed well, looked more comfortable in playing the game against a low block and we created plenty. However this defence and the goalkeeper are simply below par. Mads Hermansen needs dropping for Alphonse Areola and we need to start winning games, and quick, in order to push for an automatic promotion spot.

item.title: Germany squad gathers for training ahead of Nations League clashes
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Germany national team coach Jurgen Klopp speaks during the post-match press conference after the UEFA Nations League Group A2 soccer match between Germany and Serbia at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Germany squad gathers for training ahead of Nations League clashes») Christian Charisius/dpa All 24 players in the Germany squad, including last-minute replacement Ridle Baku, have gathered in Herzogenaurach near Nuremberg ahead of the team's last two Nations League group games. On Sunday, Klopp called up RB Leipzig right back Baku after Borussia Dortmund's Waldemar Anton was ruled out with a muscle injury. All 24 players had now arrived in Herzogenaurach for training, the German Football Federation said, ahead of Friday's match in Belgrade against Serbia, and for the match three days later in Berlin against group leaders Netherlands. Among those arriving were returning player Niclas Füllkrug of SV Werder Bremen and the 17-year-old Gladbach newcomer Wael Mohya. Goalkeeper Marc André ter Stegen, for now the number one choice in goal, is 34 years old, twice the age of Mohya. Klopp is aiming to take the national team into the Nations League quarter-finals next March after the World Cup flop last summer. To reach the quarter-finals, the DFB team would still need to move up from third place to one of the top two spots in Group B of League A. Netherlands and Greece lead the group with 8 points each, ahead of Germany on 5, who have won only one of their first four matches. This week, the DFB team is preparing for international matches for the last time at the home ground of its long-standing kit supplier Adidas. Next year, US rival Nike will take over as the new kit supplier and DFB sponsor.

item.title: England call up Burn as Guéhi pulls out of squad
item.description: FILE PHOTO - England manager Thomas Tuchel reacts during a media conference at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «England call up Burn as Guéhi pulls out of squad») Jonathan Brady/PA Wire/dpa Thomas Tuchel has recalled Dan Burn following Marc Guéhi’s withdrawal from the squad for England’s Nations League doubleheader. Tuchel’s side round off the year with Thursday’s Wembley encounter against Croatia and a trip to world champions Spain on Sunday. Manchester City defender Guéhi has featured in England’s last 15 matches but will miss those games due to a reported hip issue, which has led to Newcastle defender Burn’s first call-up since the summer. A statement from the Football Association read: "Dan Burn has been added to the England squad following the withdrawal of Marc Guéhi through injury. "The Newcastle United defender, who has 11 caps, joined up with the rest of Thomas Tuchel’s group at Tottenham Hotspur’s training ground on Monday. Guéhi was substituted at half-time of Manchester City’s fixture at Nottingham Forest on Saturday and will now remain with his club."

item.title: Flyers Game 20: Lines, Notes, & How to Watch @ Canucks
item.description: The Philadelphia Flyers (4-10-5) will look to bounce back after a disappointing loss on Sunday when they take on the Vancouver Canucks (3-15-1) at Rogers Arena. Puck drop is at 9:30 PM ET. The Cunucks enter Monday’s game after being winless in their last 5 games. On the other side of their most recent win is a 10-game losing streak. It has not been a pretty season for the Canucks. The Flyers, on the other hand, have lost 4 of their last 5 games, including 3 straight. They’re coming off a brutal 4-3 OT loss against the Flames, one where the Flyers blew 3 leads. It has been a severely underwhelming season for both team. One team has to win this game. item.description: The Denver Broncos were able to escape Charlotte with a 26-21 victory on Sunday, improving their record to 7-2 on the season. It was the team's fifth straight win. The Broncos had to make some big plays down the stretch in order to get their 16th straight victory in one-score games, a new NFL record . item.title: A tale of two matches: Rams respond to Norwich nightmare
item.description: [BBC] Derby players piled on top of Ryan Nyambe who scored his first ever career goal on his 312th professional appearance [Shutterstock] Before the Rams faced Norwich on Tuesday, the message from the fanbase was clear: Derby just needed to show some pride and provide something to believe in. They failed, miserably. Heading into half-time 3-0 down, with very little fight, character or desire shown, boos rang around Pride Park as supporters headed for the exits. With Norwich taking their foot off the gas in the second half, the Rams were probably let off the hook and lucky to only concede once more. A night to forget. Four goals conceded in back-to-back games, seven points from safety, and John Eustace's future in doubt more than ever. There had rightfully been criticism of the club from top to bottom following that result. Eustace was criticised for playing academy product Isaac Gordon at right-back, leaving him exposed, whilst the experienced Ryan Nyambe played at centre-back. A back five, or swapping Gordon and Nyambe, might have offered the youngster better protection. The players were criticised for their lack of effort. For large parts of the first half, the Rams didn't look like they were trying. Players failed to sprint back, close the ball down or make tackles. The lack of fight and belief fell well below the standards Derby County supporters expect. Finally, Stephen Pearce. From his involvement in the Mel Morris disaster - with the former owner putting the club into administration in 2021 - to questionable recruitment decisions, a constant lack of accountability for his failings, and even the current injury crisis. Supporters' frustrations with him have only grown over recent years, and have now started to reach boiling point. From kick-off on Tuesday evening until nine o'clock on Friday night, the Rams felt like a lost cause. So what changed? To start with, Eustace fielded a team with balance and trust. Nyambe returned to right-back, with Jack Robinson and Shane Duffy bringing leadership, experience and organisation to the defensive line. Mohammed Fuseini provided pace and an attacking outlet, whilst Rhian Brewster's natural technical ability made a massive difference. The players fought hard. Derby beat Bolton to ease pressure on Eustace How 'calm' Eustace got the result he needed for Derby Unlike Tuesday, the Rams worked their socks off. Tackles flew in, communication was there for all to see, and players bust a gut to track back and pressure Bolton. Despite their improved efforts, the Rams still headed into the interval a goal down. However, the comparison to Tuesday night's display gave Pride Park that belief they'd been crying out for, with many feeling Derby were still in the game. item.title: Field, format, more: What fans need to know about the 2026 Charles Schwab Cup Championship
item.description: The PGA Tour Champions season finale is here with the Charles Schwab Cup Championship. It's the culmination of not just the 28-event 2026 season but also the league's three-tournament playoff. There are subplots galore heading into the final at Phoenix Country Club in Arizona. Who's in the field? Who has a shot to win? Will there be one winner of the tournament and another winner of the season-long points race? All that and more can be answered here What is the Charles Schwab Cup Championship? The tournament, the Charles Schwab Cup Championship, is the final event of the season. Charles Schwab took over title sponsorship in 2003. It has been played at Phoenix Country Club since 2017 after previously being held at Desert Mountain Club in Scottsdale, Arizona, from 2012 to 2016. The field is also just 36, though it will be 35 this time around (details below). The Charles Schwab Cup, however, despite its similar name, is the prize for the winner of the season-long points winner. There are usually two different golfers celebrating these accomplishments. Last year was one of the exceptions as Stewart Cink claimed both titles, something that's only happened three times since 2001. 2005: Tom Watson 2012: Tom Lehman 2025: Stewart Cink Who qualified for the Charles Schwab Cup Championship 2026? The PGA Tour Champions postseason started with 72 players, got trimmed to 54 for the middle of three events and will have 36 in the final. Here's the list of 36 qualifiers: Stewart Cink Zach Johnson Steven Alker Padraig Harrington Retief Goosen George McNeill Boo Weekley Ernie Els Rory Sabbatini Darren Clarke Ben Crane Alex Cejka Jerry Kelly Soren Kjeldsen Y.E. Yang Scott Hend Darren Fichardt Miguel Angel Jimenez Tag Ridings Richard Green Tommy Gainey Freddie Jacobson Vaughn Taylor Michael Wright Cameron Percy Tim O'Neal Dicky Pride Charlie Wi Stephen Ames Steve Allan Ricardo Gonzalez Vijay Singh Matt Gogel Bo Van Pelt Thongchai Jaidee David Toms First-time winners making Charles Schwab Cup Championship debut Zach Johnson Scott Hend Ben Crane Vaughn Taylor Rory Sabbatini Darren Fichardt Who has a chance to win the season-long points title? They've crunched all the numbers and the season-long Charles Schwab Cup points title will go to one of two players: Stewart Cink or rookie Zach Johnson. Cink comes into the event in the No. 1 spot in points with Johnson No. 2. Johnson, however, leads the circuit with six wins, while Cink has five. Two-time Cup winner Steven Alker has four wins and made a hard charge down the stretch but he's stuck in third and the math didn't work in his favor to get him close enough to compete for another Cup title. Who made the final 36 but is ineligible for the Charles Schwab Cup Championship? That would be Matt Gogel, who was suspended by the PGA Tour Champions after he got popped for gambling in August.
